summary: The comment opposes tying E-Rate decisions to screen-time conditions, citing concerns about educational safety and the impact on schools' ability to protect children online if funding is reduced.

claims.argument: Screen-time limits are needed to ensure educational safety and effectiveness.
claims.evidence_quote:
--screens are often used as rewards and babysitters, which is not educational
--if the E-rate subsidy goes away, children very likely will be less safe online, and schools (which are already underfunded) will have less ability to protect kids.
